headline: Rent growth holds up, but sale timing swings profit lower
summary_short: Revenue was $194.9M, up 8.2% y/y and roughly flat q/q; diluted EPS of $0.58 rose 38.1% y/y but fell from $1.08 a quarter earlier, since Q1 booked a much larger gain on real-estate sales.
summary_long: Revenue rose 8.2% y/y to $194.9M on higher same-store rental rates and tenant recoveries plus lease-up of recently developed space, partly offset by a slight dip in same-store occupancy (94.2% vs 94.8% y/y). Same-store cash NOI grew 6.7% y/y for the quarter. Net income fell 46.1% q/q to $77.1M (still up 39.7% y/y) because Q1 booked a far larger gain on real-estate/land sales than Q2's $16.6M gain. Diluted EPS was $0.58, up 38.1% y/y but down from $1.08 in Q1. The company declared a $0.50/share dividend (+12.4% y/y), authorized a new $250M buyback that was unused this period, and held $46.1M cash plus $724.9M of undrawn revolver capacity. No forward guidance range appears in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Same-store rental rate and tenant-recovery increases plus lease-up of recently developed space drove growth, partially offset by a slight dip in same-store occupancy and lower revenue from sold properties.
Growth tracked the same rent and occupancy dynamics behind revenue, as property expenses and G&A (ex proxy-contest costs) rose more slowly than revenue.
The q/q decline is a gain-on-sale timing effect: Q1's real-estate/land-sale gain was far larger than Q2's $16.6M, implying roughly $109M landed in Q1 (H1 total $125.6M minus Q2's $16.6M).
Q2 net income fell sharply q/q (still up 39.7% y/y) purely from the smaller Q2 gain on real-estate sales versus Q1's outsized land-sale gain, not from weaker operations.

Leasing fundamentals stayed healthy (35.1% cash rent growth on new/renewal leases, 94.9% in-service occupancy per the release), while quarter-over-quarter earnings comparisons are distorted by lumpy property and land disposition gains.
